title: detect-intermittent-outage-signatures-and-bridge-traffic-guard
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: We observed multiple short-lived flapping incidents where tail latency spikes repeated in 10-30s bursts across replicas; current canary detectors raise noisy alerts and automated rollouts sometimes overreact, causing avoidable failovers. This PR adds a lightweight intermittent-outage pattern detector that identifies repeat, self-similar micro-outage signatures across slices and a bridging traffic guard that performs a controlled traffic bridge to a secondary pool while preserving canary signal for post-incident analysis. Design: detector computes a compact signature combining short-window percentile bursts, inter-spike spacing histogram, and an exponential moving autocorrelation score. A lightweight state machine maintains recent-event runs and emits a confidence score. The bridge guard policy uses a short-lived traffic siphon (5-30s) to a warm standby pool with sticky-kv-preservation and marks the original variant for deeper post-bridge evaluation instead of immediate rollback. Implementation notes: new modules under canary/detectors (outage_pattern_detector.go), canary/policies (bridge_guard.go), a python probe to surface synthetic end-to-end checks (canary/probes/bridge_probe.py), unit and e2e smoke tests, and docs+runbook. The implementation is optimized to avoid heavy histogram allocations during hot paths and relies on the existing metrics and probe infra. Commits summary: [1] initial detector core + unit tests; [2] bridge guard policy and policy wiring; [3] probe and e2e smoke; [4] docs and runbook; [5] lint fixes and test flakiness fixes. Files changed: canary/detectors/outage_pattern_detector.go, canary/policies/bridge_guard.go, canary/probes/bridge_probe.py, canary/docs/outage-detector.md, e2e/tests/outage-bridge-smoke.yml, internal/metrics/metrics_registry.go (small export), test/unit/outage_detector_test.go. CI / checks: first CI run failed on gosimple/lint and a flaky e2e timeout; lint fixes + test stabilizations were pushed and final CI passed on rerun. Performance impact: detector runs in O(n) over short fixed windows (default 60s) and adds <2% CPU overhead on canary workers in our bench; bridge guard only runs on decision path and is explicitly rate-limited. Rollout safety: the bridge guard is gated by config flags and requires two independent signals (detector confidence + synthetic probe failure) before routing traffic. Related work: complements the existing temporal-cohort and entropy-based detectors by focusing on recurrent micro-outage patterns rather than distributional drift. Linear links: ENG-15982 (detector design), ENG-16010 (bridge guard ops/rollback behavior).

review_comments: Priya Nair: Nice approach. Can you add a short note on how this interacts with the existing entropy-based canary? Also request: make the default window configurable via runtime flag.

Author (Asha Kapoor): Added runtime flag 'OUTAGE_DETECTOR_WINDOW_S' with default 60s and documented interactions w/entropy detector in outage-detector.md. The bridge only triggers if entropy detector is not in declining-signal state.
Evan Reynolds: The bridge preserves KV affinity — ensure we log a linkage ID so rollback analysis can correlate sessions across pools.
Author (Asha Kapoor): Added 'bridge_link_id' to logs and included correlation example in runbook; tests updated to assert link presence.
Jordan Lee: CI flake observed in e2e; suggestion to make probe retry deterministic in test harness.
release_notes: Add intermittent outage pattern detector and a controlled bridge traffic guard to reduce noisy rollbacks. Config flags allow tuning window and confidence thresholds. Runbook included for ops response.
notes_for_ops: Runbook added at canary/docs/outage-detector.md describing signal thresholds, how to disable bridge guard, and how to extract bridge_link_id for forensic analysis.
manual_test_instructions: 1) Enable outage detector by flipping 'OUTAGE_DETECTOR_ENABLED=true' in dev env. 2) Inject synthetic micro-outage bursts via e2e/tests/outage-bridge-smoke.yml. 3) Observe detector confidence metric 'canary.outage.confidence' and 'canary.bridge.actions' events in console. 4) Verify bridge_link_id appears in logs and that traffic is routed to standby for 5-30s.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: Non-breaking: feature gated behind flags and defaults are off for stable release. Metrics added are additive.
